headline: Plzen chase a first point against a Levski side built to defend
summary: Plzen have lost both Europa League games and sit on 0 points, so Thursday's home game with Levski Sofia already matters. Levski have conceded only 2 goals in their last five, which is the problem for a home side that won at Jablonec on Sunday while giving up 3.16 expected goals. Czech media report Kováč will change 3 starters, and Levski travel without 6 players, including defender Kamdem. Across the market Plzen are 53.7% favourites, rated 0.75 goals better, with the goals line at 2.75.
read: Plzen are at home and clear favourites at 53.7%, still chasing their first point of the Europa League campaign after two defeats in which they have conceded five goals. Levski Sofia arrive having conceded only twice in five matches, so the home side's task is turning possession into goals against a side set up to defend.

facts.fact: Plzen have lost both of their Europa League league-phase matches and go into this one with 0 points.
facts.meaning: A win here is close to essential already if the Czech side are to keep knockout-round hopes alive.

facts.fact: Plzen are 53.7% favourites to win, more than twice Levski's chance of taking the game.
facts.meaning: The market reads this as a home win more likely than not, not a coin flip.

facts.fact: Levski Sofia have conceded just 2 goals in their last five matches.
facts.meaning: The away side arrive hard to break down, which is the main obstacle to Plzen turning territory into goals.

facts.fact: Plzen's last five matches read WLWLL.
facts.meaning: No draws and three defeats — the home side have been all or nothing, and they have not strung wins together since early October.

facts.fact: Plzen won 3-2 at Jablonec on Sunday but gave up 3.16 xG in the process.
facts.meaning: The win was built on finishing rather than control — they were out-created away from home and needed three goals to get past it.

facts.fact: The market's fair handicap line is -0.67, with the main line at Plzen -0.75.
facts.meaning: The market expects a home win by around a goal — a controlled Plzen night rather than a rout.

facts.fact: Plzen's last five matches have produced 17 goals.
facts.meaning: Games involving the home side have been high-scoring at both ends, which shapes the goals market.

facts.fact: Plzen head coach Radoslav Kováč plans three changes to his starting lineup and says he wants to win against Levski at all costs.
facts.meaning: A reshuffled home eleven is expected, with the coach turning up the pressure after two European defeats.

sources.fact: Plzen head coach Radoslav Kováč plans to make three changes to the starting lineup compared with the last match against Levski Sofia.
Kováč says he believes his team will confirm its improvement in performance and results after the international break.
Plzen are seeking their first points of the Europa League league phase after losing their opening two matches, and a win would revive their hopes of reaching the knockout rounds.
Ferencváros beat Plzen at home in the Europa League a week before this match, according to Hungarian Conservative.
Three current Plzen players arrived at the club from Levski Sofia in the recent past, Plzeňský deník reports.
Kováč is described as wanting to win against Levski at all costs, according to Czech Television.
Levski Sofia's recent defensive solidity is highlighted ahead of the match against Plzen, according to DailySports.
